content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "counterexample", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "The quoted Lemma is stated in full generality for any pairwise-intersecting family of nonempty finite sets. Take F_k={x_0,...,x_k,y_k}, k>=0, all distinct symbols; every two members share x_0, so the hypothesis holds. T_n={y_0,...,y_{n-1},x_n} is a transversal (y_k hits F_k for k<n; x_n hits F_k for k>=n) and is minimal: deleting y_j misses F_j, deleting x_n misses F_n. So there are infinitely many distinct inclusion-minimal finite transversals. If the conclusion held, each B_j would itself be a transversal, so every minimal transversal equals some B_j, giving at most s of them - contradiction. The induction's flaw is visible: the criterion only covers transversals meeting C, yet it is applied to F_c whose transversals need not meet C\\{c}. Finiteness (F) rests entirely on this lemma, so the proof fails."}
